title: feat(generate-text): steps
body:
I use `while` instead of recursion, decreasing the risk of stack overflow.

Meanwhile, I removed chain calling and replaced it with liner code.
author: luoling8192

comments.body:
> Thanks for the Contribution! I prefer to use recursion.

Some notes here (not enforcements):

While recursion is indeed the underlying nature of `for`, `while` no matter from the semantics or implementation perspective views. And yes, as any regular algorithm would do, recurision will always be the first thing to consider. IMO, I would say with recursion, there are several things we might missed to consider with:

1. Potential Stack Overflow issues
2. Use of `while` or other types of `for` variant can be seen as "flatten" operation for developers to maintain, ready it easier.
3. Easy to return, easy to continue, easy to break, with better flexibilities and scalabilities.
  - (Special case) perhaps allow function hooks of function callings to return or early return in special cases
  - (Special case) perhaps easier to say `-1` or `undefined` for infinite steps?
